newsitem.title: FINLAND: Nokia drives Helsinki up as Ericsson shines.
newsitem.headline: Nokia drives Helsinki up as Ericsson shines.

text.p: Shares rose on Thursday, with bourse-engine Nokia powering up in heavy trade after Swedish rival Ericsson reported first-half pre-tax earnings up 44 percent and above analysts' forecasts.

The 20-share FOX index rose 0.57 percent to 1,209.23, setting an intraday life-high 1,228.19, but ending some 11 points short of its previous July 17 peak close. The all-share HEX index rose 1.15 percent to 3,508.84 points.
Volume was again massive, at over a billion markka, more than half in Nokia. But brokers said the day's gains looked fragile after a soft U.S. open.
"The market was up, but the increase came almost entirely from Nokia and Merita," one broker said, adding: "If the U.S. market ends down, there will be more profit-taking tomorrow."
After a hesitant start, Nokia jumped on the Ericsson report and ended up 18.00 markka at 443.00, but off an intraday high 456.00, which was just two markka short of its all-time high.
Brokers and analysts said Ericsson's earnings performance showed the mobile phone market, in particular, is still growing fast and some said they would up their forecasts for Nokia.
Merita extended recent gains, closing up 1.00 markka at 24.30 after posting a life-high 24.50 in lively trade.
Brokers said some profit-taking hit other segments of the market, especially forestries.
UPM-Kymmene fell 1.40 markka to 132.10, Enso dropped 1.30 to 48.00, and Metsa-Serla lost 1.50 to 43.00.
Out of the limelight it grabbed last week, Raisio fell 15.00 markka to 595.00, back below 600 at the close for the first time since July 17.
Raisio soared after announcing on July 15 that it had reached a deal with U.S. consumer goods giant Johnson & Johnson's McNeil unit to market its Benecol cholesterol-cutting agent in North America.
